punchline: Matthew Syed says one ordinary road in England produced more top table tennis players than the rest of the country combined for a spell in the 1980s.
thirty_sec: Matthew Syed grew up on an ordinary road in south-east England and became England's top table tennis player. For a stretch in the 1980s his street produced more outstanding players than the rest of the country combined. A teacher who was England's top coach recruited him and his brother to a club with 24-hour access, and they played for hours. Syed admits he might have been just another player without that.
